name: Southwest Houston Pilot (Harris / Fort Bend)
description: Bounded pilot study area in southwest Houston spanning Alief, Sharpstown, Westchase, Mission Bend, Stafford, Missouri City and east Sugar Land, across the Harris County / Fort Bend County line. Includes the Brays Bayou and Keegans Bayou watersheds, which flooded during Tropical Storm Allison (2001) and Hurricane Harvey (2017).
selection_rule: Census tracts (2020 vintage, TIGER/Line 2024) whose Census internal point falls inside selection_bbox. The study-area polygon is the union of those tracts; road and facility data cover the study-area bounds plus road_buffer_m to limit edge effects.
justification: FEMA flood hazard polygons (FIRM database, DFIRM 48157C) were retrievable for the Fort Bend portion during Phase 1; the official FEMA NFHL service is configured as the primary source for the full area.
Contains both Harris County (48201) and Fort Bend County (48157) tracts, so the multi-county data model is exercised from day one.
Dense, well-mapped OpenStreetMap road network with freeways (I-69/US-59, Beltway 8, Westpark Tollway), arterials and local streets.
Large populations with documented transportation and income barriers (Alief, Sharpstown, Gulfton edge).
Small enough (about 18 x 18 km) for fast local processing and Phase 2 routing experiments.
